owner_acknowledgements.topic: Kill tiers: multi_kill carries tier 2-5 (own kills in the window) and streak carries tier 3-10 (kills since the last own death). A package may bind one clip per tier; lookup takes the highest bound tier not above the occurrence, and an untiered binding covers every tier.
owner_acknowledgements.channel: Owner reply in the engineering chat session about announcer packs ("add tiers")
owner_acknowledgements.scope: Tier dimension in EVENT-AUDIO-SPEC section 2 and bindings[].tier in section 7 only; taxonomy 1.1 and media-manifest 1.2.0. Does not approve DEC-EVENT-AUDIO as a whole, any package content or any licence.

owner_acknowledgements.topic: The event set and kill counting follow Dota 2 itself: multi-kill is a chain with at most 18 s between consecutive own kills, and streak is the game's count of kills since the last own death. Events of other games with no Dota 2 equivalent (for example smackdown or annihilation in a Heroes of Newerth pack) are not catalog events and cannot be bound.
owner_acknowledgements.channel: Owner reply in the engineering chat session about announcer packs ("follow Dota 2 as the reference")
owner_acknowledgements.scope: Counting semantics and catalog scope of multi_kill and streak in EVENT-AUDIO-SPEC section 2 only. Detector assumptions E-3 and E-4 stay unconfirmed until a capture shows them.

decisions.blocks: Account, friend code and sign-in design (SOCIAL-001..003, PEER-007, PEER-009 and the proposed ACCOUNT-001 to ACCOUNT-010)
decisions.channel: Owner message in the engineering chat session (2026-11-12): Fable 5.2 reviews, the lead follows; see docs/design/ACCOUNT-IDENTITY-REVIEW.md
decisions.decision: Kohbor has its own account system that copies the G-Maiden pattern and shares nothing with it (new broker, database, Google client, signing key and friend-code format). Sign-in is Google only through the system browser with loopback redirect and PKCE, scope openid only; no email is requested or stored and the provider subject is kept only as a keyed hash; no password and no Kohbor recovery flow; players without Google stay guests. Public identity is a random rotatable Kohbor friend code plus a display name; search is by exact code only. No Steam link or Steam login in the first release. Tokens are native-only under OS user-scoped protection. The choice was delegated by the owner to an independent agent review (not a human, security or legal review): docs/design/ACCOUNT-IDENTITY-REVIEW.md section 1.
decisions.remaining_decision: Owner to confirm: Google as the only first-release sign-in, that non-Google users stay guests, no recovery flow, and the session and limit values.
decisions.safe_interim: Build the client and relay interfaces against the review; nothing is hosted until DEC-ACCOUNT-ORIGIN and DEC-PRIVACY-LEGAL close. Sign-in stays optional (DEC-SIGNIN-OPTIONAL).
decisions.closure_evidence: ACCOUNT requirements added to the SRS; product-identity labels frozen; contract tests for token audience, pair-secret pairing and delete-without-tombstone.

decisions.blocks: Audio-only announcer packs (MP-03, MP-04, media-manifest 1.3.0) and the owner's existing WAV-only clip sets
decisions.channel: Owner message in the engineering chat session (2026-11-12): chose the middle path after the lead explained audio-only bindings and the split between voice and banner packs
decisions.decision: One package type. A binding may omit its silent video: an audio-only binding plays its audio, shows no banner and declares visual_tail_ms 0; a binding with a video is paired by event key inside the same package and the author guarantees the timing. Audio is verified exactly as before. No banner is invented when none exists. Store SKUs may be sold as voice-only and voice-plus-banner without a second format.
decisions.safe_interim: Implement media-manifest 1.3.0 in kohbor-pack, the authoring tool and the fixtures; the host already treats a missing visual url as no banner.
decisions.closure_evidence: Reader, store, authoring tool and fixtures accept and verify audio-only bindings; hostile and install tests updated; spec text amended.

decisions.blocks: Banner add-on packages that extend a voice package, and mix-and-match of a voice and a banner from different packages
decisions.safe_interim: Not built. Pairing happens inside one package only; descriptors reference visuals by binding so a later extends field can be added.
decisions.closure_evidence: A decision on the extends rule, the timing contract between a banner and a voice it was not authored with, two active selections in the registry with their leases and fences, critical readiness for each, and the authority of each package.

decisions.blocks: The look, motion style and production pipeline of announcer and system event banners
decisions.channel: Owner message in the engineering chat session (2026-11-13) after previewing both banner lab results: adopt the Fable 5.2 result
decisions.decision: Adopt the Fable 5.2 banner lab result as the baseline for event banners: pre-rendered 3D-animated silent WebM (VP9 with alpha, 1280x480, 30 fps) whose Thai text is the sentence the announcer says, stamped in step with the voice, plus an original synthesised sound-effect bed mixed into the package WAV; the pipeline is a WebGL2 renderer in headless Edge piped to the pinned ffmpeg, rebuilt by one command. The ASTRA (gpt-6-astra) result is not adopted. This decision does not approve DEC-VISUALS tokens, does not authorise any clip as critical media (DEC-CRITICAL-MEDIA), and does not settle rights to the VRZO voice.
decisions.safe_interim: Lab outputs stay outside the repository (they contain the VRZO voice, whose rights are an unverified owner claim); no banner file is shipped or committed.
decisions.closure_evidence: Owner auditions the mixed audio; owner confirms the Thai sentence of every banner (first_blood, match_start and hero_kill use unverified automatic transcripts and the lab changed two tokens); the banners are played in the real overlay (WebView2 VP9 alpha) with a measured decode cost; tier scaling for multi_kill 4 and 5 and streak 3 to 10; the font licence (Leelawadee UI Bold, a Windows system font) is checked; the renderer source is reviewed before it enters the repository.
